passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The investigators returned from Canada.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities said Bowman was expected to be deported to the United States within approximately two weeks.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators planned to question him further after his return.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The investigation into his van remained unresolved because the vehicle was still in Canada.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman remained in Yellowknife awaiting deportation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators from the FBI, Virginia and North Carolina planned to meet him after he was returned to the United States.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators also planned another trip to Inuvik to obtain access to and search Bowman’s van through the appropriate Canadian procedures.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman continued stating that he would cooperate with investigators.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman was ordered detained so a grand jury could question him.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators returned to Canada to inspect Bowman’s van for forensic evidence.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Garrison “Gary” Bowman, a retired carpenter from Mayodan, North Carolina, was released from the Roanoke City Jail after a federal magistrate determined there was no longer a basis to keep him detained as a material witness.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman had been returned from Canada and detained on a federal material-witness warrant connected to the Short investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: During the hearing, federal prosecutor Tony Anderson told the court that Bowman had cooperated with federal authorities and that investigators no longer considered him a flight risk.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: U.S. Magistrate Judge Glen Conrad concluded that the material-witness warrant against Bowman was legitimate. However, he found that federal authorities had not said or done anything intended to make people believe Bowman had committed the Short murders.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman remained scheduled to testify before a federal grand jury on November 12, 2002.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman continued to deny involvement in the murders of Michael and Mary Short or the abduction and murder of Jennifer Short.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman told reporters after his release that when the matter was over, “you’re going to get both barrels.”

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: His attorney, William Cleveland, said Bowman intended to change the public’s perception of him once he could legally discuss the investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: A federal magistrate dismissed the material-witness warrant and released Bowman from custody after federal prosecutors said he had cooperated with investigators and there was no longer a reason to detain him. He was required to appear before a federal grand jury on November 12, 2002, to answer additional questions concerning the Short investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Federal authorities detained him under a material-witness warrant connected to the Short investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: A material-witness warrant did not accuse Bowman of committing the murders. It allowed authorities to secure testimony from someone considered important to the investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators questioned Bowman extensively.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman Returned to the United States: Bowman was eventually returned to the United States after his detention in Canada.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Federal Grand Jury: Bowman testified before a federal grand jury investigating the Short case.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators continued describing him as a witness of interest rather than announcing him as the killer.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities said they still wanted to communicate with him and resolve outstanding questions. Bowman continued denying involvement.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators returned from Canada with items collected from Bowman’s van.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators submitted the evidence to the forensic laboratory in Roanoke, Virginia, for examination.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The van itself remained in Canada.
